paper_title: Constraints on axion-like dark matter from a SERF comagnetometer
suggested_experiment_name: NASDUCK-SERF (Noble And Alkali Spin Detectors for Ultralight Coherent darK matter - Spin-Exchange Relaxation-Free comagnetometer)
coupling_convention: g_an (dimensionless axion-neutron coupling), as plotted on y-axis
notes: Paper reports constraints on both ALP-neutron (g_aNN) and ALP-proton (g_aPP) couplings. The primary new result is the first reliable terrestrial bounds on ALP-proton coupling, but the abstract and title emphasize the neutron constraint as well. Figure 2 shows detailed exclusion limits as functions of mass. The bounds are presented as 95% C.L. exclusion regions (bright red bands in Fig. 2). Extracting precise numerical values from the figure is difficult due to finite resolution; the paper states bounds are tabulated in Ref. [57]. The abstract mentions improvements of 'up to two orders of magnitude for neutrons' and 'over two orders of magnitude for protons' in the mass range 1.4×10^-12 to 2×10^-10 eV. The coupling convention in the paper is g_aNN and g_aPP in units of GeV^-1. Since the paper presents both neutron and proton couplings with comparable emphasis, and the pre-analysis hint suggests AxionProton, there is ambiguity. However, the title and abstract lead with 'neutron and proton' couplings equally, and the paper's main innovation is the first reliable proton bounds. Given the coupling_type enum requires a single choice and the paper constrains BOTH, I select AxionNeutron as the primary result (left panel of Fig. 2 is the neutron constraint), but note that AxionProton is equally valid. The extraction confidence is reduced to 0.65 due to this ambiguity and the difficulty in reading precise numerical values from the figure.
